description: Ramayana correspondences in the Hindi mythological film 'Bajrangbali' (1976, dir./prod. Chandrakant, Dara Singh as Hanuman; 170 min; music Kalyanji-Anandji, lyrics Kavi Pradeep). CAPTION PASS DONE (2026-10-02): scenes located against the film's Hindi auto-caption track (ASR, mediocre on 1970s devotional Hindi) — locators are scene-level windows; the cleaned transcript is committed as the source-of-record (bajrangbali-1976-transcript.jsonl) because YouTube regenerates auto-captions over time. Known caption gaps: the 01:40–02:07 climax stretch is song-heavy and ASR yields no name hits there, so the Ravana-vadha scene itself is not caption-locatable; Sulochana is never spelled by ASR. Anchors stay at kanda/sarga level per board choice.

target.numbering_notes: kanda/sarga in the Gita Press 1970s reprint numbering (= ramayana.info numbering); GP scans are the bindery archive.

entries.episode: Hanuman's birth and childhood: son of Anjani (Durga Khote) and Kesari, with Vayu as spiritual father; child Hanuman's leap at the rising sun and the Indra-vajra jaw wound.
entries.notes: Film evidence: cast credit Durga Khote as 'Devi Maa Anjani'; IMDb 'Vanar family tale: Pawan and Anjani's son'. The leap at the sun IS Valmiki (Uttara 34-36); the swallowing-the-sun variant is later vernacular — the film follows the vernacular telling per genre convention. Birth-of-Hanuman content absent from Valmiki's first six kandas; hence uttara anchor. Captions: Anjani addressed at 00:10:32; the childhood/gurudakshina thread 00:10:26–00:12:43; Anjani first named 00:04:07.

entries.quote: शबरी मां तुम्हारी बहू सीता को कोई / अनाचारी पंचवटी से उठा लेगा (00:22:35)
entries.episode: Shabari's hermitage: the aged ascetic woman (Dulari) receives Rama and offers tasted fruit.
entries.notes: Film evidence: cast credit Dulari as Shabari. The tasted-fruit detail beloved of the film tradition is aranya 74-78 (GP numbering; content-check pending). Captions: single explicit Shabari naming at 00:22:35, with a Panchavati-abduction reference in the same breath — the film compresses the forest sequence here; single-line evidence, scene match plausible not certain.

entries.quote: जिसकी पूंछ में आग लगाकर छोड़ दिया जाए (01:00:03)
entries.episode: Hanuman's tail set on fire by Ravana's guards (Moolchand credited as 'Ravan's guard, setting Bajrangbali's tail on fire'), followed by Hanuman burning Lanka.

refs.verified_against: ramayana.info sundara/53,54 (tail set fire to it; burning mansions)

entries.notes: Film evidence: explicit cast credit. Ramayana anchor content-verified; in GP numbering the tail-fire + burning of the city fall in sundara 53-54. Captions: Hanuman in Ravana's court ~00:57:27; explicit tail-fire dialogue 01:00:00–01:00:06.

entries.episode: Kumbhakarna (Asit Sen) awakened, rampages, and falls to Rama.
entries.notes: Film evidence: cast credit Asit Sen as Kumbhakarna. Slain in GP yuddha 67-71 (content-check pending). Captions: name invoked repeatedly at 01:12:47 (the waking call), immediately after a Meghnad mention at 01:12:33 — the war-council/awakening sequence.

entries.quote: लक्ष्मण की मृत्यु हुई हमारे इंद्रजीत की श्रद्धांजलि (01:29:37)
entries.episode: Meghnath/Indrajit (Randhawa) in battle with the serpentine noose and astras; his queen Sulochana (Jayshree Gadkar); Indrajit slain by Lakshmana.
entries.notes: Film evidence: cast credits Randhawa as 'Rajkumar Meghnath', Jayshree Gadkar as 'Rajkumari Sulochana'. The nagapasha binding is GP yuddha 47-49; the slaying is 87-90 (verified). Sulochana and the widow's grief thread are NOT in Valmiki — vernacular (Rama-charit-manas and later) material; her scenes are the film's own interpolation beyond Valmiki though Indrajit himself is Valmiki's, hence beyond_valmiki=false for the entry with the Sulochana caveat here. Captions: Meghnad named 01:12:33; the shakti-strike aftermath 'Lakshmana has died by our Indrajit's...' 01:29:37. Sulochana never spelled by ASR (song scenes) — her thread rests on the cast credit.

entries.quote: संजीवनी बूटी मिले / द्रोणाचल पर्वत पर है / सूर्योदय से पहले आ जानी चाहिए (01:29:25)
entries.episode: Ravana mortally wounds Lakshmana; Hanuman lifts the whole Sanjivani mountain (IMDb: 'brings forth the Sanjeevani herb, along with the entire mountain, and Laxman gets a second life').

refs.verified_against: scene detail (Dronachal mountain, before-sunrise deadline) matches the Valmiki episode; yuddha/90-adjacent Indrajit context verified at ramayana.info yuddha/90

entries.notes: Film evidence: IMDb plot outline. Valmiki has the wound (Indrajit's shakti/brahmastra) and the mountain brought whole (GP yuddha 73-76); the film's dramatic emphasis on Hanuman carrying the mountain matches the tradition. Content-check pending. Captions: dense scene 01:29:25–01:30:35 (10 hits) with the Dronachal + sunrise details — textbook match, hence high.

entries.quote: धोबी के मुंह में कीड़े पड़े उसने / तो सीता जी को भी कलंक लगा दिया (02:07:43)
entries.episode: Ravana's fall with Vibhishana's help (IMDb: 'Ten-headed Ravan is killed with Vibhisan's [Ravana's brother's]...'), then — per cast — the Uttara-kanda coda: the dhobi's quarrel (Ram Mohan), Sita's banishment, and the Lava-Kusha boys (Ajay, Master Alankar) with the asvamedha horse.
entries.notes: Film evidence: IMDb outline + cast credits Ram Mohan as 'Dhobi, washerman', Ajay as Luv, Master Alankar as Kush. The dhobi slander and Sita's banishment = GP uttara 42-48 (the HOL-259 fascicle's own sargas; numbering verified there); the Lava-Kusha asvamedha recitation and battle sit in the uttara tail (GP numbering for those sargas pending a check — 'various'). Vibhishana's counsel is Valmiki (yuddha 6-19); the slaying is 98-107 (106 verified). Captions: dhobi slander 02:07:43–02:08:54 with the agni-pariksha reference at 02:08:39 ('even after the fire ordeal the people of Ayodhya…'); Shatrughna at 02:21:03 opens the asvamedha thread; the horse-confrontation 'क्या नाम है तुम्हारे पिता का' 02:47:33 + 'do not treat us as children' 02:47:36 = Luv-Kush vs the army. The Ravana-vadha scene sits in the 01:40–02:07 song-heavy stretch where ASR yields no name hits — scene present per cast/plot but not caption-locatable.
